narrative.summary: Kyrgyzstan regulates AI through Chapter 23 of its Digital Code (Code No. 178 of 31 July 2025, in force from early 2026), a risk-based regime under which owners assess the hazard of their AI systems, AI systems of increased danger must meet mandatory requirements and carry a published declaration of conformity, and interactions with AI and deepfakes must be disclosed; the Code replaced the 2008 personal information law. The Cabinet of Ministers has adopted the implementing rules: Resolution No. 770 of 2 December 2025 sets requirements for hazard-assessment methodologies and for risk management, characteristics, data quality and technical documentation of increased-danger AI systems, and Order No. 1181-t of 31 December 2025 sets the content and form of the conformity declaration. A draft AI ethics regulation and a draft AI development concept from the digital ministry have not yet been published in a form that could be read.
lead_institutions: State Agency for Personal Data Protection
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed on 12 and 18 October 2026: national laws and Cabinet acts in the Ministry of Justice legal database, the parliament, the personal data agency, the National Bank and the public-discussion portal were searched. Not yet verified from the official text: material of the digital ministry, including the draft AI ethics regulation and AI concept, which are still pending as leads.

instruments.english_title: Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic
instruments.issuing_authority: Jogorku Kenesh of the Kyrgyz Republic
instruments.current_status: Code of 31 July 2025 No. 178, listed as in force (edition of 31.07.2025) in the Ministry of Justice central legal database, published in the official newspaper Erkin-Too of 8 August 2025 No. 59. Law of 31 July 2025 No. 179 "On bringing into force the Digital Code" (published in Erkin-Too of 5 August 2025 No. 58) brings the Code into force six months after that publication and repeals among others the Law "On personal information" of 14 April 2008 No. 58, the Law "On electronic governance" and the Law "On electronic signature"; the legal database lists 6 February 2026 as the entry-into-force date of Law No. 179, but the Code's own entry-into-force day is not printed, so no commencement date is given. The Cabinet of Ministers set the AI hazard-assessment requirements in Resolution of 2 December 2025 No. 770 and the AI conformity declaration in Order of 31 December 2025 No. 1181-t. A Kyrgyz-language official version exists on the same database.
instruments.summary: Code of 31 July 2025 No. 178 consolidating rules on the digital environment, digital services and systems, digital identity, personal data and telecommunications. Chapter 23 (Articles 191-197) sets principles for AI systems (risk reduction, openness, explainability, human control, accuracy, reliability, security), prohibits AI designed to deliberately and unlawfully harm protected interests, and requires every owner to assess the danger of its AI system and publish the result and methodology. Owners of "increased-danger" AI systems must run lifecycle risk management, keep documentation and logs and sign a published conformity declaration before use (requirements and declaration form set by the Cabinet of Ministers); users must ensure human oversight and explain AI-assisted decisions affecting rights, and providers must disclose AI interactions, emotion-recognition/biometric categorisation and deepfakes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding horizontal AI rules (the Code also replaced the 2008 Law on personal information and created a special-regulation sandbox regime) in Kyrgyzstan: risk-based duties for owners and users of AI systems, transparency and deepfake labelling.
instruments.publisher_name: Jogorku Kenesh of the Kyrgyz Republic

instruments.summary: Kyrgyzstan's first personal data protection law (No. 58 of 14 April 2008, as amended in 2017 and 2021), regulating the collection, processing and use of personal data by state bodies, local governments and legal entities on the basis of international principles. It set rules for personal data arrays and their holders, data subject rights and cross-border transfer, and barred merging personal data arrays collected for different purposes for automated processing. It was repealed by Law No. 179 of 31 July 2025 when the Digital Code (Chapter 11 on personal data) entered into force.

instruments.english_title: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution of 2 December 2025 No. 770 approving requirements for the methodology for assessing the hazard of artificial intelligence systems and requirements for increased-danger artificial intelligence systems
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic
instruments.current_status: Listed as in force in the Ministry of Justice central legal database; published in the official newspaper Erkin-Too of 5 December 2025 No. 96 (3753). It enters into force fifteen days after the Digital Code enters into force (paragraph 4); the exact day is not printed. Adopted under Articles 193 and 194 of the Digital Code.
instruments.summary: Cabinet resolution adopted under Articles 193-194 of the Digital Code that approves five sets of requirements: for the methodology owners use to assess the hazard of AI systems, and for risk management, system characteristics (openness, explainability, controllability, accuracy, reliability, digital resilience), data quality and technical documentation of increased-danger AI systems. It requires all owners of AI systems used in Kyrgyzstan to assess hazard at each lifecycle stage using their own methodology meeting the requirements (covering harm to life and health, rights and freedoms, the environment, defence, national security and public order) and, where a system is classed as increased-danger, to maintain a lifecycle risk-management system and publish its technical documentation on their websites.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main implementing regulation for the Digital Code's risk-based AI regime: sets how AI hazard is assessed and the mandatory requirements for increased-danger AI systems.

instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic
instruments.current_status: Listed as in force in the Ministry of Justice central legal database. It enters into force fifteen days after the Digital Code enters into force (paragraph 3); the exact day is not printed, so no commencement date is given. Adopted under Article 195 of the Digital Code.
instruments.summary: Cabinet order adopted under Article 195 of the Digital Code that approves the required content of, and a standard form for, the declaration of conformity of increased-danger AI systems with the Code's mandatory requirements. Before putting such a system into use, its owner must confirm conformity by adopting a declaration in this form (stating accuracy, reliability, digital resilience, openness, explainability and controllability, the test report, the hazard-assessment methodology used and where technical documentation is available) and publish it on its website as a digital document signed with a qualified digital signature, openly accessible.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets the mandatory self-declaration of conformity that owners of increased-danger AI systems must publish before use under the Digital Code.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Kyrgyzstan were searched, including the Digital Code and other laws, Cabinet resolutions, ministries and regulators. No qualifying material was found for strategy, government AI governance, ethics, public-sector AI, procurement, cyber-security, standards, readiness indexes, sectoral rules, drafts or international instruments. Items known only from the press, such as Resolution No. 770 of 2 December 2025, a draft AI ethics regulation and a national AI concept, remain leads to check.
